summary: On the first day (Saturday), we focused on researching places similar to the Moon and Mars, as well as checking if those locations matched their temperatures, environment, whether the soil is rocky, has a clay-like texture, etc. We also planned to create an interactive game to "have a better experience and give more depth to our project," so that it wouldn't just be a presentation—in other words, something that had an interactive variable. On day two (today/Sunday), we focused on fixing errors in the presentation and giving it a nicer aesthetic, as well as improving the game so it would have more features and people could enjoy the experience more.
details:
Mission Analogs: Moon and Mars is a 3D simulator that runs in a web browser with no installation. Players explore 12 real places on Earth that resemble the Moon or Mars, such as the Tatacoa Desert, the Atacama Desert, Utah and Iceland. There they operate replicas of real space equipment like rovers, the lunar module and Ingenuity, complete missions, and manage their energy in a habitat.

It's accessible, with a spoken tutorial, route guidance and plain-language help. It's inclusive, working in five languages with voice narration. Players learn by doing, and it's accurate: it cites its sources and never makes up data.

Its value lies in showcasing the places where space agencies train for the Moon and Mars. These places are little known, and some are in Latin America. The simulator brings science closer to anyone and could spark interest in STEM careers.
dataRefs: Diviner maps lunar surface temperatures and provides especially useful products for studying the lunar poles. Its polar and resource products could be compared with extreme cold, ice-bearing, or other terrestrial environments.
